title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is not a Grothendieck manuscript. It is a typed page, numbered -32-, from the preprint of Serre–Tate, 'Good reduction of abelian varieties' (Annals of Math. 88, 1968), §7 on abelian varieties with complex multiplication. It sits among Grothendieck's crystalline notes. The neighbouring pages are handwritten French notes on crystalline and infinitesimal topoi and on divided-power envelopes over Witt vectors.

Setting: A is an abelian variety of dimension d over a number field K with complex multiplication by a CM field F, [F:Q] = 2d. By Th.11 of the paper, the Galois action on Tate modules gives a continuous homomorphism ε: I_K → F^*. On finite idèles it is locally constant. On principal idèles x ∈ K^* it agrees with the algebraic 'type' ψ (a reflex-norm-type map), with ψ_∞: (R⊗K)^* → (R⊗F)^* its archimedean extension.

One sets ρ_∞(a) = ε(a)·ψ_∞(a_∞^{-1}). For x ∈ K^* we have ε(x) = ψ(x) = ψ_∞(x_∞), so ρ_∞ is trivial on K^*. It equals ε on the idèles with trivial infinite component. It is continuous, since ψ_∞ is continuous and ε is locally constant on the finite part. These properties characterize ρ_∞.

For any embedding σ: F → C, the composite χ_σ = (1⊗σ)∘ρ_∞: I_K → C^* is a Hecke character (Grössencharakter) with values in C^*. Up to normalization it is the Shimura–Taniyama character ([18], p.148). Its restriction to the local units U_v is σ∘φ_v, where φ_v: U_v → F^* is the local character from Th.6. Since σ is injective, ker(σ∘φ_v) = ker φ_v, so the local conductor exponent of χ_σ equals n_v.

After extending scalars, V_ℓ(A) splits into 2d one-dimensional pieces, one for each embedding of F, and each has conductor exponent n_v. Hence the conductor exponent of A at v is 2d·n_v (Th.12). In particular, the bad-reduction set equals the support of the conductor of χ_σ. This generalizes Deuring's result for CM elliptic curves.
errors: No mathematical errors. The step 'exponent of the conductor of A at v = 2d·n_v' tacitly uses that V_ℓ is free of rank 1 over F⊗Q_ℓ, so that over an algebraic closure it splits into 2d characters σ∘φ_v of equal conductor. This is established earlier in the paper (Th.6 and its proof).

ideas.what: Construction of the C^*-valued Hecke character χ_σ attached to a CM abelian variety from the ℓ-adic idèle-class homomorphism ε and the infinity type ψ_∞
ideas.modern_name: Hecke character (algebraic Grössencharakter) of a CM abelian variety; Shimura–Taniyama / Serre–Tate
ideas.where_published: Serre–Tate, Good reduction of abelian varieties, Ann. of Math. 88 (1968), §7

ideas.what: Conductor of a CM abelian variety equals the 2d-th power of the conductor of its Hecke character; bad reduction set equals support of the conductor
ideas.modern_name: Serre–Tate Theorem 12 (conductor of CM abelian varieties)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a preprint page of Serre–Tate's published 1968 Annals paper (Theorem 12), filed among Grothendieck's crystalline notes. The content is fully published and credited. Its only interest is archival: it shows Grothendieck held the Serre–Tate preprint alongside his crystalline work.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate.
The page is typed English, not Grothendieck's hand; the handwritten '3' at the bottom left is an archive pagination mark.
The page number '-32-' is the preprint's own pagination.
